title: Sparse Matrix Operations
spec: Write a function called `multiply(matrices)` that takes a list of two sparse matrices. Each matrix is a dictionary mapping coordinate tuples to numbers. Create a dense representation of the first matrix by finding the maximum row and column indices. Loop over the rows and columns to fill in the values. Perform a standard matrix multiplication with the second sparse matrix, iterating through rows, columns, and the inner dimension. Finally, analyze the resulting matrix by iterating through its contents to find the maximum value, the sum of all values, and the set of unique column indices that contain non-zero entries. Return a tuple containing the final matrix, the maximum value, the sum, and the unique columns. Example input: a list containing two dictionaries with coordinates mapped to ones.

title: Inverted Index Builder
spec: Write a function called `index(documents)` that takes a dictionary mapping document titles to strings of text. Split each text into words. Build an inverted index mapping each word to a dictionary that tracks the frequency of that word in each document. Iterate through the documents and their word frequencies to populate this structure. Generate a simulation over thirty consecutive days, artificially increasing the frequency of every word slightly each day. For each word in the final index, extract the documents containing it and their corresponding frequencies. Compute the total occurrences of each word across all documents by gathering the frequency numbers and mapping pairs. Return the complete inverted index and the final word counts. Example input: a dictionary with three short titles mapped to simple sentences.

title: Dependency Task Scheduler
spec: Write a function called `schedule(tasks)` that takes a dictionary mapping task names to lists of prerequisite task names. First, calculate the in-degree of every task by traversing the dependencies. Iterate through all available tasks to find those with zero prerequisites, adding them to a queue. Assign each processed task to a consecutive time slot up to a maximum of thirty days. Generate a daily log showing which tasks are executed on each day. Analyze the daily log by iterating through its contents to compute the total tasks executed, the list of active days, and the highest daily task count. Return the daily log and the active days. Example input: a dictionary of five tasks with linear dependencies.

title: Warehouse Inventory Aggregator
spec: Write a function called `aggregate(shipments)` that takes a list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a daily shipment containing product names mapped to quantities. Create a master inventory tracking the total quantity of each product across all days. Process a forecasting simulation for a standard ninety day quarter, where daily usage reduces the inventory of each product by a fixed percentage. Build a restocking plan that flags products dropping below a threshold during the simulation period. Review the final master inventory to extract all product names, all final quantities, and specific product to quantity pairings for a final audit report. Return the master inventory and the restocking plan. Example input: a list of three shipment dictionaries with fruit names and numbers.

title: Network Routing Costs
spec: Write a function called `route(network)` that takes a dictionary mapping city names to dictionaries of neighboring cities and travel costs. Calculate the shortest path from a starting city to all other cities using a priority queue. Iterate through the network to discover all available cities and all unique connections. After finding the shortest paths, simulate a series of fifty delivery runs starting from the source city, increasing a base cost each run. Summarize the network by gathering the list of all destination cities, the individual costs to reach them, and the complete mappings of cities to their shortest path costs. Return the shortest paths and the total cost of all delivery runs. Example input: a dictionary representing a triangle of three cities with integer edge weights.

title: Image Contrast Enhancement
spec: Write a function called `enhance(image)` that takes a list of lists of integers representing pixel intensities from zero to two hundred fifty five. Calculate the frequency of each intensity value across the entire image. Compute the cumulative distribution of these frequencies by accumulating the counts sequentially from zero up to two hundred fifty five. Map the old intensities to new values using the cumulative distribution to equalize the histogram. Apply this mapping to the original image grid by traversing its rows and columns to create an enhanced image. Extract the unique intensity values present in the new image and their final occurrence counts. Return the enhanced image grid and the final frequency statistics. Example input: a three by three grid of integer pixel values.

title: Tournament Bracket Simulator
spec: Write a function called `simulate(teams)` that takes a dictionary mapping team names to their numerical skill ratings. Determine the number of tournament rounds required by calculating the base two logarithm of the number of teams. Create a schedule for each round, pairing teams sequentially. In each match, compare the skill ratings and advance the team with the higher rating. Track the total matches played by each team. Once the tournament concludes, analyze the results to find the overall winner, list all participating teams, compile the final win counts for each team, and display the full pairing history. Return the winner and the statistics. Example input: a dictionary of four teams and their integer ratings.

title: Applicant Job Matching
spec: Write a function called `match(applicants)` that takes a dictionary mapping applicant names to lists of acceptable job titles. Implement a matching algorithm to assign as many applicants to jobs as possible without assigning the same job twice. To do this, attempt to find an augmenting path for each applicant. Keep track of the job assignments as a dictionary mapping jobs to applicants. Afterward, project the staffing schedule over fourteen days, where each assigned applicant works a standard shift. Generate a summary extracting all filled jobs, all hired applicants, and the pairs of successful assignments. Return the assignment mapping and the fourteen day schedule. Example input: a dictionary of three applicants and their preferred job lists.

title: N-Gram Text Generator
spec: Write a function called `generate(corpus)` that takes a list of text strings. Build a bigram transition model mapping each word to a dictionary of subsequent words and their transition counts. Iterate through the transitions to convert the counts into probabilities. Use the model to generate a new sequence of exactly fifty words, starting with the most frequent initial word. To ensure diversity, occasionally fall back to a random word from the vocabulary. Extract the complete vocabulary, the set of all subsequent word frequencies, and the exact transition pairs from the model. Return the generated sequence and the transition model. Example input: a list of two short sentences.

title: Cipher Frequency Decryptor
spec: Write a function called `decrypt(message)` that takes a string of encrypted uppercase text. Generate all twenty six possible decrypted messages by applying shifts from zero to twenty five. For each shifted message, count the frequency of each letter. Compare these frequencies against a standard English letter distribution to calculate a penalty score for each shift. Select the shift with the lowest penalty score. Process the best message to extract its individual character counts, the list of unique characters present, and the raw frequency values. Return the successfully decrypted message and its character statistics. Example input: a short string of encrypted uppercase text.

title: Cargo Loading Optimizer
spec: Write a function called `optimize(cargo)` that takes a dictionary mapping item names to tuples containing weight and monetary value. Set a maximum weight capacity of fifty units. Create a dynamic programming table to determine the maximum value achievable for every weight limit from zero up to the maximum capacity. Trace back through the table to identify the specific items included in the optimal solution. Compile a manifest of the loaded items, their individual values, and the total value. Extract the names of the selected items and their corresponding weight and value pairs. Return the maximum value and the manifest. Example input: a dictionary of four items mapped to weight and value tuples.

title: Grid Puzzle Validator
spec: Write a function called `validate(grid)` that takes a nine by nine grid of integers. Check each of the nine rows and each of the nine columns to ensure they contain every number from one to nine exactly once. Then, divide the grid into nine three by three subgrids and verify the same condition for each subgrid. Maintain a tracking dictionary that counts how many times each number appears in the entire grid to ensure no missing values. Review the tracking dictionary to retrieve the numbers, their total counts, and the mapping pairs. Return a boolean indicating whether the grid is a valid solution, along with the tracking dictionary. Example input: a completely filled nine by nine puzzle grid of integers.

title: Directory Size Analyzer
spec: Write a function called `analyze(files)` that takes a dictionary mapping absolute file paths to file sizes in bytes. Reconstruct a hierarchical directory tree where each folder maps to its subfolders and files. Traverse the file paths by splitting them into segments and navigating the tree up to a maximum depth of twenty levels. Calculate the total size of each directory by summing the sizes of its direct files and recursively adding the sizes of its subdirectories. Generate a report for the top ten largest directories. Extract all directory names, all computed sizes, and the directory size mappings from the final tree. Return the directory tree and the size report. Example input: a dictionary of five file paths and integer sizes.

title: Grid Population Simulator
spec: Write a function called `simulate(population)` that takes a list of coordinate tuples representing living entities. Establish a grid bounded by the minimum and maximum coordinates of the population. Run a simulation for exactly one hundred generations. In each generation, count the number of living neighbors for every cell in the bounding box by checking adjacent horizontal, vertical, and diagonal positions. Apply survival rules to determine the living entities for the next generation. After the simulation, summarize the final grid by collecting all living entity coordinates, the final counts of neighbors for those coordinates, and the complete mapping of entities to their neighbor counts. Return the final population coordinates. Example input: a list of three coordinates forming a simple blinker pattern.

title: Image Compression Encoder
spec: Write a function called `compress(image)` that takes a list of lists of integers representing pixel colors. First, transpose the image by swapping rows and columns across the dimensions. Flatten the transposed image into a one dimensional sequence. Traverse the sequence to group consecutive identical colors, replacing them with a count and the color value. Organize the compressed data into a dictionary mapping block indices to their count and color. Calculate the compression ratio by extracting the block indices, the sequence of color values, and the full pairs of compressed blocks. Return the compressed dictionary and the block statistics. Example input: a two by two grid of ones and zeroes.

title: Optimal Prefix Coder
spec: Write a function called `encode(text)` that takes a string of characters. Count the frequency of every character in the string. Build a priority queue of characters and their frequencies to construct a binary tree. Traverse the tree to assign a binary sequence to each character, based on its path from the root. To simulate transmission, construct a timeline of sixty discrete intervals and place encoded characters into the timeline sequentially. Extract the original characters, their corresponding binary codes, and the complete dictionary mapping characters to codes. Return the encoded text and the binary code mapping. Example input: a short repeated word.

title: Corporate Salary Aggregator
spec: Write a function called `aggregate(employees)` that takes a dictionary mapping employee names to their individual salaries and their direct manager. Build a hierarchical structure mapping each manager to a list of their subordinates. Compute the total payroll responsibility for each manager by summing their own salary and the salaries of their entire reporting chain. Project the payroll growth over the next five years, applying a standard annual raise to all salaries. Collect all manager names, all calculated payroll totals, and the detailed mappings of managers to their totals. Return the payroll mapping and the five year projection. Example input: a dictionary of four employees with their salaries and assigned managers.

title: Sequential Word Predictor
spec: Write a function called `predict(words)` that takes a list of strings representing a sequence of words. Construct a transition matrix that maps each word to a secondary dictionary containing the counts of words that immediately follow it. Use this matrix to simulate a conversation spanning fifty turns. For each turn, select the next word based on the highest transition count from the current word. Evaluate the transition matrix to extract the unique preceding words, the frequency dictionaries of succeeding words, and the exact pairs of words and their transitions. Return the simulated conversation and the transition matrix. Example input: a list of ten alternating words.

title: Currency Combination Calculator
spec: Write a function called `calculate(coins)` that takes a list of integer coin denominations. Determine the number of ways to make exact change for every amount from zero up to one hundred. Initialize an array to store the combinations for each amount. For each coin denomination, update the combinations array by adding the previous ways to reach the current amount. Construct a dictionary mapping each amount to its number of combinations. Review the final dictionary to retrieve the distinct amounts, the counts of combinations, and the exact pairings of amounts and combinations. Return the dictionary and the combination count for one hundred. Example input: a list of three standard coin integer values.

title: Highway Traffic Simulator
spec: Write a function called `simulate(vehicles)` that takes a dictionary mapping vehicle identifiers to their starting positions on a linear highway. Run a traffic simulation for exactly one hundred twenty time steps. In each time step, advance each vehicle by one position unless the position ahead is occupied. Maintain a speed log recording the total distance covered by each vehicle. After the simulation, summarize the traffic flow by gathering all vehicle identifiers, their final accumulated distances, and the complete mappings of vehicles to their final positions. Return the final vehicle positions and the speed log. Example input: a dictionary of three vehicles and their initial integer positions.

title: Player Ranking Calculator
spec: Write a function called `rank(matches)` that takes a list of tuples containing the winning player name and the losing player name. Initialize a rating dictionary assigning a standard starting score to every unique player found in the match history. Process each match sequentially to adjust the ratings based on the outcome. Group the players into ten separate ranking tiers by iterating from one to ten based on their final scores. Extract the names of all ranked players, the lists of players in each tier, and the specific mappings of players to their final numerical ratings. Return the tier groupings and the final rating dictionary. Example input: a list of five match outcomes between three distinct players.

title: Server Workload Allocator
spec: Write a function called `allocate(requests)` that takes a dictionary mapping user names to their requested compute time. Divide an available server cluster into twenty four hourly time slots. Distribute the requested compute time evenly across the available slots for each user. Identify any slots where the total allocated time exceeds the server capacity and cap the allocations proportionally. Compile a billing report that includes all user names, their total fulfilled compute times, and the exact mappings of users to their hourly allocations. Return the hourly distribution and the billing report. Example input: a dictionary of three users and their requested integer compute times.

title: One Dimensional Clustering
spec: Write a function called `cluster(points)` that takes a list of integer coordinates. Select three initial centroid positions. Run an optimization loop for exactly twenty iterations. In each iteration, assign every point to the nearest centroid, forming clusters. Recalculate the positions of the centroids by averaging the points assigned to them. Store the final clusters in a dictionary mapping the centroid positions to the lists of their assigned points. Evaluate the final clustering to extract the centroid locations, the groups of clustered points, and the detailed mappings of centroids to points. Return the cluster dictionary and the final centroids. Example input: a list of ten scattered integer coordinates.

title: User Similarity Recommender
spec: Write a function called `recommend(ratings)` that takes a dictionary mapping user names to dictionaries of movie titles and their numerical ratings. Calculate the similarity between a target user and all other users by finding the difference in ratings for shared movies. Select the most similar user and identify movies they rated highly that the target user has not yet seen. Project these recommendations over the next ten movie nights. Extract all movie titles from the system, all the similarity scores computed, and the specific mappings of users to their similarity scores. Return the recommendations for the target user and the similarity mappings. Example input: a dictionary of three users with overlapping movie ratings.

title: Calendar Event Merger
spec: Write a function called `merge(events)` that takes a dictionary mapping calendar dates to lists of scheduled meeting durations. Map the meeting times into a continuous hourly timeline covering exactly forty eight hours. Identify overlapping meetings and combine them into single blocks of continuous occupied time. Calculate the total free time available by analyzing the merged blocks. Extract the individual dates, the sequences of merged meeting blocks, and the precise pairings of dates with their finalized schedules. Return the merged event dictionary and the total free time. Example input: a dictionary with two calendar dates and overlapping meeting durations.

title: Stock Portfolio Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(portfolios)` that takes a list of portfolios, where each portfolio is a dictionary mapping stock symbols to shares owned, along with a historical price dictionary mapping symbols to lists of thirty daily prices. The function must return a list of thirty daily total values for all portfolios combined. To do this, calculate the total value of each portfolio for each day by iterating through the numerical days, checking that the symbol exists in the price records. Find which stock contributed the most to the overall value on the final day, and the average daily value of the entire market. Include a helper function to calculate a single portfolio daily values, and a main routine that creates sample dictionaries and loops through them to print the results.

title: Regional Weather Aggregator
spec: Create a function `aggregate(records)` that processes weather data represented as a dictionary mapping region names to dictionaries of station names and their monthly temperature lists. The function must calculate the annual average temperature for each station, the maximum temperature recorded in each region, and a list of regions that had missing data. Use an index loop to iterate through the twelve months of data for the annual calculations. Produce a list of tuples containing region statistics and extract all unique station names from the mappings. Include a helper to compute station averages and a small driver block with sample data that iterates through the output to display it.

title: Theater Seating Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(requests)` that assigns seats in a theater with a specific number of rows and seats per row given as plain integers. The requests are a dictionary mapping group names to the number of people. The function must iterate through the numeric rows and seats to find consecutive empty spots for each group. Keep track of the assigned seats internally. Return a list of tuples for the assignments, a list of unaccommodated groups, and the total number of empty seats remaining by scanning the seating grid. Add a short main block that defines a theater of ten rows and twenty seats, processes five sample requests and loops over the assignments to print them.

title: Social Network Analyzer
spec: Write a function `examine(network)` where the network is a dictionary mapping user names to lists of their friends. The function should find all users who have no mutual friends with their own friends, and also calculate the average number of friends across the network. Include a helper function that takes a user and the network to determine their mutual friend count by checking all pairs of their friends using an index loop. Produce a tuple containing the list of isolated users, the most popular user, and the network average. Demonstrate the logic with a small driver block that generates a sample network dictionary and iterates over the results.

title: Flight Network Analyzer
spec: Implement `route(flights)` that takes a dictionary mapping departure cities to dictionaries of destination cities and ticket prices. The function must identify all isolated cities that have inbound flights but no outbound flights by comparing the departure and destination mappings. It should also find the cheapest direct flight in the entire network and generate all valid three city travel itineraries. Use a loop with a fixed count of three to construct the multi city paths. Return a list of isolated cities, the lowest price found, and a list of the paths. Include a sample flight network and a call to the main function to display the options using a loop.

title: Election Vote Tabulator
spec: Design a function `tabulate(regions)` that takes a dictionary mapping region names to dictionaries of candidate names and their vote counts. Calculate the total votes for each candidate across all regions by combining the nested mappings, and identify the overall winner. Find any candidate who received zero votes in at least one region, and generate a list of the top three regions with the highest total voter turnout. Write a helper to compute a single region total, and use a small main section to set up sample voting data and execute the tabulation, iterating over the final tallies to print them.

title: University Course Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(availability)` that assigns courses to weekly time slots based on instructor preferences. The availability is a dictionary mapping course names to lists of acceptable time slot numbers. The schedule spans forty possible slots. Iterate through the courses and their mappings to assign each to its first available preferred slot, ensuring no two courses share a slot. Return a list of tuples pairing courses to their assigned slots, a list of unassigned courses, and a count of unused slots by looping through all forty slots. Include a short sample program that creates preferences for five courses and prints the resulting schedule by iterating over the assigned slots.

title: Recipe Batch Scaler
spec: Create a function `scale(recipes)` which accepts a dictionary mapping recipe names to their ingredient requirements, where each requirement is a dictionary of ingredient names and base quantities. The program must scale all quantities to produce five batches of each recipe, using a numerical loop for the batches. Calculate the total shopping list required for all recipes combined, and identify which single ingredient appears in the most recipes by analyzing the requirement mappings. Return the master shopping list as a list of tuples and the most common ingredient. Include a helper to scale a single recipe and a driver section to run a sample scenario and print the list item by item.

title: System Log Analyzer
spec: Implement a function `parse(logs)` that processes a dictionary mapping server names to dictionaries of error types and their occurrence counts over a day. The function must calculate the total errors per server and flag any server exceeding a threshold of fifty errors. It should also aggregate the total counts for each error type across the entire infrastructure and identify the most frequent error by examining the combined mappings. Return a list of flagged servers and the overall most frequent error type. Use a driver section to construct a sample log mapping and loop through the output to report anomalies.

title: Menu Profitability Calculator
spec: Write a function `appraise(menu)` where the input is a dictionary mapping dish names to dictionaries containing their selling price and a dictionary of ingredient costs. The function must calculate the profit margin for each dish by subtracting the sum of ingredient costs from the price. Determine the average profit margin across all dishes, and find all dishes whose total ingredient costs are higher than their selling price. Return a list of unprofitable dishes and the highest profit margin dish. Provide a main block to instantiate a small sample menu and demonstrate the evaluation by iterating over the returned statistics.

title: Property Portfolio Valuator
spec: Design a function `price(properties)` taking a dictionary mapping property identifiers to dictionaries of features such as area, age, and condition score. The function should calculate an estimated valuation for each property using a base rate multiplied by the area, discounted by the age, and boosted by the condition score over a projection of five years using a numerical loop. Identify the average age of all properties, the identifier of the most expensive property, and a list of properties with a perfect condition score. Include a helper to score a single property and a main block that evaluates a sample property portfolio and loops through the prices.

title: Document Anagram Grouper
spec: Write a function `group(documents)` that takes a dictionary mapping document names to lists of words. The function must find all anagrams across all documents by sorting the characters of each word to form a signature, repeating this for the first twenty words of each document using an index loop. Build a dictionary mapping these signatures to lists of the original words. Identify the longest list of anagrams, the signatures that appear in multiple documents, and calculate the total number of unique signatures. Return the largest anagram group as a list of words and the count of unique signatures, and include a driver block with sample document texts that prints each group.

title: Ancestry Tree Analyzer
spec: Implement a function `trace(lineages)` where the input is a dictionary mapping parent names to lists of their children. The function must compute the total number of descendants for each parent up to three generations deep. Iterate through the exact generation levels using a numeric loop. Identify parents who appear in the mappings but have no grandchildren, and find the maximum number of children any single parent has. Return a list of parents without grandchildren and the highest child count. Write a helper function for the depth traversal and a small main block to test a sample family tree and iterate over the descendants.

title: Retail Cart Discounter
spec: Create a function `discount(carts)` taking a dictionary mapping customer names to their shopping carts, where each cart is a dictionary of item names and prices. The function must apply a progressive discount to the first five items in each cart, using a numerical loop to adjust the discount rate based on the item position. Calculate the final total for each customer, and find the total revenue across all carts by combining the mappings. Identify any items that were purchased by every customer. Return a list of final customer totals and the shared item names, providing a sample input in a main execution block that loops over the final totals.

title: Telemetry Threshold Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(telemetry)` that takes a dictionary mapping sensor names to lists of twenty hourly readings. The function must analyze the readings to find any sensor that exceeds a critical value for three consecutive hours, using an index loop to check the sequences. Calculate the average reading for each sensor and extract all unique reading values recorded across the system from the mappings. Return a list of alerting sensors and the highest average reading. Include a helper to scan a single sensor reading array and a sample driver block to iterate through the alerts.

title: Playlist Duration Fitter
spec: Design a function `fit(library)` where the library is a dictionary mapping artist names to dictionaries of song names and their durations in seconds. The function must construct a playlist by taking the first three songs from each artist, tracking the selection order using a numeric loop. Calculate the total duration of the resulting playlist and collect all artists from the mappings who have fewer than three songs available. Return the final playlist total time and the list of artists with insufficient songs. Add a main block with a sample library to test the selection and loop through the final sequence.

title: Regional Tax Calculator
spec: Implement a function `calculate(orders)` taking a dictionary mapping state names to dictionaries of product categories and total sales amounts. The function must apply specific tax rates to each category for a period of four quarters, using a numerical loop for the periods, computing the total tax owed per state. Find the average tax collected across all states, and identify states that had zero sales in at least one category by checking their mappings. Determine the product category that generated the most tax overall. Return a list of tuples with state tax totals and the top category, including a sample driver block that iterates over the totals.

title: Workout Milestone Tracker
spec: Create a function `track(workouts)` where the input is a dictionary mapping user names to lists of their daily step counts for a four week period. The function must calculate the weekly total steps for each user by dividing the twenty eight days into four segments using an index loop. Identify users who improved their step count every single week, and calculate the overall average steps per day across all users from the provided mappings. Return a list of consistently improving users and the global daily average. Include a helper to process a single user and a driver block to iterate and print the milestones.

title: Library Penalty Calculator
spec: Write a function `penalize(records)` that takes a dictionary mapping patron names to dictionaries of borrowed book titles and days overdue. The function must calculate the fine for each book based on the days overdue, capping the penalty at a maximum of fourteen days using a numeric loop to increment the daily fine. Aggregate the total fine for each patron, and identify all books that are overdue by more than ten days across the entire library by checking the nested mappings. Return a list of tuples with patron totals and the severely overdue books list. Include a sample execution block that loops over the severe fines.

title: Moving Average Smoother
spec: Implement a function `smooth(streams)` that accepts a dictionary mapping device names to lists of fifty numeric measurements. The function must compute a five point moving average for each device, using a numeric loop to access the measurement positions. Calculate the maximum smoothed value for each device, and find the global minimum across all original measurements in the mappings. Return a list of smoothed data arrays and the device with the highest peak. Include a helper function for the moving average logic and a small driver program to iterate and print the results.

title: Genomic Motif Finder
spec: Design a function `process(sequences)` taking a dictionary mapping sample names to string representations of genetic data. The function must extract all substrings of length six from each sample using a position loop, and count their frequencies. Find the most common substring for each sample, and identify any substrings that appear in every single sample by comparing their mappings. Calculate the average length of the provided sequences. Return the common substrings and the sample maximums, including a main block to run the analysis on a set of sample strings and display the findings by looping over the common strings.

title: Delivery Network Analyzer
spec: Write a function `assess(deliveries)` where the input is a dictionary mapping warehouse names to dictionaries of destination stores and distances. The function must find the average distance from each warehouse to its stores, and identify all stores that are served by multiple warehouses by examining the overlapping mappings. Find the warehouse with the highest number of destination stores, and simulate five delivery routes for each warehouse using a numeric counter loop. Return a list of tuples for average distances and the shared stores, providing a sample network to test the execution and print the shared stores one by one.

title: Auction Bid Resolver
spec: Create a function `resolve(auctions)` taking a dictionary mapping item names to dictionaries of bidder names and their bid amounts. The function must determine the winning bidder for each item by finding the maximum bid in the mappings. Calculate the total revenue if all items are sold, and simulate a five minute countdown for the final item using a numerical loop. Identify any bidder who placed bids on more than three different items. Compute the average bid amount across all auctions. Return a list of tuples pairing items to winners and the highly active bidders. Include a main section that defines a small auction scenario and iterates over the winners.

title: Factory Machine Monitor
spec: Write a function `observe(factory)` that takes a dictionary mapping production line names to dictionaries of machine names and their operating temperatures. The function must calculate the average temperature for each production line, and identify any machine exceeding an eighty degree threshold. Simulate ten cooling cycles for the overheated machines using a numerical loop, recording the temperature drops. Return a list of the overheated machines and the line averages, adding a main driver block with sample factory data that iterates through the output to demonstrate the monitoring.

title: Hotel Occupancy Forecaster
spec: Design a function `forecast(bookings)` taking a dictionary mapping hotel names to dictionaries of room types and reserved counts. The function must calculate the total reservations for each hotel and find the average number of bookings per room type across all hotels by examining the nested mappings. Project the occupancy for the next seven days using a numeric loop that applies a daily cancellation rate. Identify any hotel that currently has zero reservations. Return a list of tuples for hotel totals and the seven day projections, including a main block to instantiate sample data, execute the forecast and loop over the projections.

title: Traffic Network Congestion
spec: Write a function `simulate(network, vehicles, steps)` to model city traffic. The network parameter maps intersection identifiers to lists of neighbor identifiers. The vehicles parameter maps intersection identifiers to current car counts. Loop exactly steps times to advance the simulation. Inside, loop over a sequence from zero to three to model traffic light phases. Iterate through all intersections and their car counts in the vehicles mapping to calculate flow and divide cars equally among neighbors. Extract all the intersection identifiers from the network mapping to ensure they exist in the newly calculated mapping. Examine all the neighbor lists in the network mapping to count dead ends. Review all intersections and their updated car counts in the new mapping to verify calculations. Evaluate all the car counts in the new mapping to find the maximum congestion. Gather all the intersection identifiers from the vehicles mapping to log the active participants. Return a list of tuples containing the step index and the highest congestion found.

title: Server Resource Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(servers, tasks, rounds)` to distribute computing jobs. The servers parameter maps server identifiers to their available memory. The tasks parameter maps task identifiers to their required memory. Loop exactly rounds times to attempt allocations. Inside, loop over a priority sequence from zero to nine to process tasks in order. Iterate through all servers and their capacities in the servers mapping to find where tasks can fit. Extract all the server identifiers from the servers mapping to check system health. Examine all the available memory capacities in the servers mapping to calculate the total remaining space. Review all tasks and their requirements in the tasks mapping to see which ones are still unassigned. Evaluate all the task requirements in the tasks mapping to find the most demanding job. Gather all the task identifiers from the tasks mapping to build a final report. Return a mapping of servers to assigned tasks.

title: Economy Market Simulator
spec: Write a function `trade(merchants, prices, turns)` to model a simple economy. The merchants parameter maps merchant identifiers to their inventory mappings of goods to quantities. The prices parameter maps goods to their unit prices. Loop exactly turns times to simulate trading days. Inside, loop over a trading sequence from zero to five representing market hours. Iterate through all merchants and their inventories in the merchants mapping to produce new goods. Extract all the good names from the prices mapping to ensure all commodities are tracked. Examine all the unit prices in the prices mapping to find the most valuable item. Review all merchants and their calculated wealth in a temporary wealth mapping to apply daily taxes. Evaluate all the quantity values in every inventory mapping to calculate total market volume. Gather all the merchant identifiers from the merchants mapping to register active traders. Return a mapping of merchants to their final wealth.

title: Biological Cell Automaton
spec: Write a function `evolve(grid, generations)` to simulate cellular growth. The grid parameter maps coordinate tuples to state integers. Loop exactly generations times to advance the simulation. Iterate over the keyword dictionary keys to apply specific formatting color codes, and iterate through the matched dictionary values to identify the most used syntax construct. Use a loop over a sequence of string indices to check for unclosed string literals character by character. Iterate over the final token dictionary items to combine adjacent identical tokens, and iterate over the final token dictionary keys to extract unique tags.

title: Car Rental Fleet Manager
spec: Write an entry function `manage(reservations)`. Input is a list of booking tuples containing customer, car type, and duration, outputting a dictionary mapping car types to utilization rates. A helper function tracks daily usage by looping over a sequence of days from one to thirty. Iterate over the reservation list using a sequence of indices to process bookings, and iterate through the fleet dictionary items to check for overbooking instances. Iterate over the fleet dictionary keys to initialize the availability reports, and iterate over the utilization dictionary values to flag severe vehicle shortages. Use a loop over a sequence of discount tiers from one to four to apply promotional pricing to underutilized cars. Finally, iterate over the final report dictionary items to print the monthly results.

title: Bicycle Sharing Balancer
spec: Write an entry function `balance(stations)`. Input is a dictionary mapping location names to current bike counts, and output is a list of transfer instructions. A helper function calculates the system average by iterating over the station dictionary values. Use a loop over a sequence of transfer rounds from one to ten to simulate iterative balancing. In each round, iterate through the station dictionary items to find locations with surplus and deficit. Iterate over the station dictionary keys to form source and destination pairs, and use a loop over a sequence of truck capacities from one to three to simulate moving the bikes. Iterate over the instruction dictionary items to compile a route map, and iterate over the instruction dictionary values to calculate total distance driven.

title: Cinema Ticket Pricing
spec: Write an entry function `calculate(bookings)`. Input is a dictionary mapping customer types to quantities, and output is the total revenue based on a dictionary of base ticket prices. A helper function iterates through the booking dictionary items to multiply quantities by prices. Use a loop over a sequence of row numbers from one to twenty to assign seats logically. Iterate through the price dictionary values to find the maximum possible ticket cost for VIP upgrades, and iterate through the price dictionary keys to list available discount categories. Use a loop over a sequence of combo meal indices from zero to five to add concession sales to the order. Iterate over the final receipt dictionary items to print a detailed breakdown, and iterate over the receipt dictionary values to calculate the final tax amount.

title: Cloud Storage Tiering
spec: Write an entry function `tier(files)`. Input is a dictionary mapping filenames to days since last access, outputting a dictionary mapping storage tiers to lists of filenames. A helper function defines the tier limits by iterating over a configuration dictionary items. Iterate through the file dictionary keys to check file extensions against a whitelist, and iterate through the file dictionary values to categorize each file's age. Use a loop over a sequence of archive levels from one to three to assign cold files to deep storage incrementally. Iterate over the tier dictionary values to calculate total bytes saved, and use a loop over a sequence of chunk indices from zero to ten to simulate uploading data in blocks. Finally, iterate over the final transfer dictionary items to generate a system log.

title: Meteorological Rainfall Interpolator
spec: A meteorological station records daily rainfall, but some days are missing. The entry point `interpolate(measurements)` accepts a dictionary mapping integer days to rainfall amounts. Create a continuous list of rainfall amounts from day zero up to the maximum day present. To do this, find the maximum day by extracting the keys from the dictionary. Evaluate each day using a sequence from zero to the maximum. If a day is present, use its amount. If not, scan backwards and forwards to find the nearest valid days and compute their interpolated average. If day zero is missing, assume it has zero rainfall. Next, create an inverted grouping: group the days from zero to the maximum into a new dictionary where the integer part of the rainfall is mapped to a list of days. Count the number of days in each group by iterating through its values. Finally, calculate the average of all originally recorded amounts by iterating over the dictionary values. Return a tuple containing the continuous list, the inverted dictionary, and the average.

title: Assembly Bulk Costing
spec: Calculate bulk production costs for composite items. The entry function `pricing(components, assemblies)` takes a dictionary mapping basic component names to unit costs, and a dictionary mapping assembly names to recipes (a mapping of component names to quantities). First, verify all parts are available by iterating through the assemblies and checking if any recipe component is missing from the component keys. If a part is missing, ignore that assembly. For valid assemblies, iterate over them and their recipes to calculate the base unit cost by summing component costs. Then, generate a bulk discount table. For each valid assembly, compute total costs for batch sizes by iterating over a sequence from ten up to one hundred in increments of ten. For every full ten units, apply a cumulative one percent discount. Also, extract a sorted list of all distinct base component unit costs by iterating through the component values. Return a tuple with a dictionary of assembly pricing lists and the sorted base costs list.

title: Board Game Path Scorer
spec: Compute final scores for players moving along a linear board. The function `score(board, rolls)` receives a dictionary mapping square indices to point values, and a dictionary mapping player names to a sequence of dice rolls. First, calculate the total available points by iterating through the board values and summing them. Also, collect all defined square indices by extracting the board keys. Iterate through the players and their rolls to simulate movement, advancing their position starting from zero. If they land on a defined square, add those points. Additionally, grant a movement bonus: calculate the bonus by iterating over a sequence of steps from five up to their final position in increments of five, adding two points per step. Return a tuple containing a list of player names and scores ordered by score descending, the total available points, and the list of square indices.

title: Classroom Grade Normalizer
spec: Normalize student grades using a maximum average curve. The function `curve(grades)` accepts a dictionary mapping student names to sequences of numerical assignment scores. First, compile a list of all enrolled student names by extracting the keys from the dictionary. For every student, drop their lowest score and compute the average of the remainder. Find the highest average among all students by iterating through these computed averages. The curve is the difference between one hundred and this maximum average. Iterate through the dictionary items to apply this curve to each student's average. Also, generate a performance histogram by iterating through score brackets using a sequence from zero to one hundred in steps of ten, counting how many curved averages fall into each bracket. Return a tuple containing the curved averages dictionary, the histogram list, and the list of enrolled student names.

title: Bank Loan Amortization
spec: Generate twelve month loan amortization schedules. The function `amortize(loans, rates)` takes a dictionary mapping identifiers to principals, and a dictionary mapping identifiers to annual interest rates. First, sum the total starting principal by iterating through the loan values. Next, identify all high interest loans by iterating through the rate keys and checking if their rate exceeds zero point one. Process each loan by iterating over the loans dictionary items. For each loan, compute the monthly balance by iterating over a sequence of months from one to twelve. Each month, add interest (annual rate divided by twelve times principal) and subtract a payment of one hundred, clamping the balance to zero if it goes negative. Return a tuple containing a dictionary of schedules, the total starting principal, and the list of high interest loan identifiers.

title: Debate Team Matchmaker
spec: Pair debate teams into multiple rounds based on skill levels. The function `match(teams)` maps team names to numerical skill ratings. First, extract all team names by iterating through the input keys. Find the highest skill rating by iterating through the input values. Sort the teams by their skill rating descending. Create pairings for five distinct rounds by iterating over a sequence from one to five. In each round, shift the pairings: the team with the highest skill pairs with the team at the index equal to the round number. Sequentially pair the remaining teams by iterating over the remaining indices. If there is an odd number of teams, the last team gets a bye. Return a tuple containing the list of five round pairings, the list of original team names, and the highest skill rating.

title: Elevator Passenger Simulator
spec: Model an elevator delivering passengers to their destination floors. The function `simulate(passengers, top)` receives a dictionary mapping starting floors to sequences of requested destination floors, and the top floor integer. Identify all floors with waiting passengers by extracting the keys. Find the highest requested destination floor by iterating through all passenger sequences in the values. Start the elevator at floor one. Move up by iterating over a sequence of floors from one to the top. Then move down by iterating over a sequence from the top minus one to one. Board passengers at their start floor and drop them off when the current floor matches their destination. Keep a running list of how many people exit at each floor during the entire journey. Return a tuple containing the drop off counts per floor, the floors with waiting passengers, and the highest requested destination.

title: Chemical Isotope Mass Calculator
spec: Calculate the mass of chemical molecules and their multiples. The function `masses(elements, molecules)` takes a dictionary mapping element symbols to atomic masses, and a dictionary mapping molecule names to their composition (element symbol to count). Sum the total mass of all individual distinct elements by iterating through the elements values. Extract all known element symbols by iterating through the elements keys. Iterate over the molecules and their compositions to compute the base mass of each molecule. Then, generate a sequence of total masses for quantities by iterating over a sequence from one to five. Return a tuple containing a dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of their five masses, the total atomic mass of all distinct elements, and the list of known element symbols.

title: Secret Code Permuter
spec: Encrypt a text message using a progressively shifting substitution cipher. The function `encode(mapping, message)` accepts a dictionary mapping characters to replacement characters, and a string message. Extract all base characters by iterating through the mapping keys. Compile a list of all distinct replacement characters by iterating through the mapping values. Encrypt the message by iterating over the characters using a sequence of their index positions. For each character, find its base replacement; if missing, keep it unchanged. Apply a positional shift based on its integer index position in the message, advancing it through the alphabet and wrapping around if necessary. Also create a reverse lookup by iterating over the mapping items to map replacements back to originals. Return the encrypted message string, the reverse lookup dictionary, and the distinct replacement list.

title: Airline Luggage Fees
spec: Calculate excess luggage fees for airline passengers. The function `fees(bags)` takes a dictionary mapping passenger names to sequences of baggage weights. List all passenger names by extracting the keys. Find the heaviest single bag recorded across all passengers by iterating through all bag sequences in the values. Process each passenger by iterating over their items. For each passenger, calculate fees by evaluating their bags one by one using an index sequence. The first bag is free, the second costs fifty, and subsequent bags cost one hundred. Any bag over twenty kilos adds a twenty five dollar penalty. Finally, categorize all bags by weight bracket by iterating over a sequence of thresholds from zero to forty in steps of ten. Return a tuple with the passenger fee dictionary, the weight bracket counts, and the heaviest bag weight.

title: Sewing Pattern Resizer
spec: Scale coordinates for garment sewing patterns. The function `resize(pattern)` receives a dictionary mapping garment piece names to sequences of horizontal and vertical coordinate pairs. List all piece names by extracting the keys. Find the maximum horizontal coordinate across the entire original pattern by iterating through the coordinates in the values. Create multiple scaled versions of the pattern by iterating over a sequence of size multipliers from one to five. For each size, iterate over the garment pieces and multiply all coordinates by the current size multiplier. Store the new pieces in a dedicated dictionary for that size. Return a tuple containing a list of the five scaled dictionaries, the list of piece names, and the maximum horizontal coordinate.

title: Book Paginator Index
spec: Build a book index mapping words to page numbers. The function `paginate(words, size)` takes a dictionary mapping distinct words to a sequence of character positions, and an integer characters per page. Extract a list of all distinct words by iterating through the keys. Transform the character positions into page numbers by dividing by the page size and adding one. Collect all distinct page numbers generated by iterating through the transformed values. Format the output for a fixed ten page booklet by iterating over a sequence of pages from one to ten. For each page, collect all words that appear on it and sort them alphabetically. Return a tuple containing the booklet (a list of ten lists of words), the distinct words list, and the list of all distinct page numbers.

title: Farm Irrigation Planner
spec: Estimate agricultural water usage for a week. The function `irrigate(crops, fields)` receives a dictionary mapping crop names to base daily water requirements, and a dictionary mapping field identifiers to crop names. List all defined crop names by extracting the keys. Extract the unique crop base requirements by iterating through the crop values. Calculate the water needed for every field by iterating over the fields items. The base requirement changes each day based on a weather multiplier that starts at one point zero and increases by zero point one daily. Compute the total water for each field by iterating over a sequence of seven days and applying the multiplier to the crop's base requirement. Return a tuple containing the field totals dictionary, the defined crop names, and the unique base requirements.

title: Volunteer Kiosk Roster
spec: Assign volunteers to a thirty day schedule kiosk. The function `roster(volunteers)` accepts a dictionary mapping volunteer names to sequences of available integer days. List all volunteer names by extracting the input keys. Build the schedule by iterating over a sequence of days from one to thirty. For each day, iterate through the volunteers to find who is available. Assign the volunteer with the fewest scheduled days so far, breaking ties alphabetically. If no one is available, assign empty. Keep track of total assigned days per volunteer. Finally, calculate the maximum number of days assigned to any single person by iterating through the totals dictionary values. Return a tuple containing the thirty day schedule list, the list of volunteer names, and the maximum assigned days.

title: Museum Tour Guide Assignment
spec: Assign museum tour guides to daily visitor groups. The function `schedule(groups)` maps arrival hours to visitor counts. Identify all hours that have expected visitors by extracting the keys. Calculate total daily visitors by iterating through the values and summing them. The museum operates from nine to eighteen. Iterate over a sequence of operating hours from nine to eighteen. If an hour has visitors, allocate one guide for every ten visitors rounded up. Maintain a running tally of allocated guides. Collect the required guides per hour into a list. Return a tuple containing the guide allocation list, the list of hours with visitors, and the total daily visitors.

title: Music Chord Progression Generator
spec: Generate musical chord progressions by shifting frequencies. The function `chords(notes, steps)` takes a dictionary mapping note names to base frequencies, and an integer steps. List all note names by extracting the keys. Collect all base frequencies by iterating through the values. Iterate over the notes and their frequencies to construct a three note chord using multipliers of one, one point five, and two. Generate progressions for each chord by multiplying all three frequencies by a sequence of scale factors. Create these factors by iterating over a sequence of numbers from zero to the steps input, converting them to factors starting at one and incrementing by zero point one. Return a dictionary mapping note names to their generated chord sequences, the note names list, and the base frequencies list.

title: Typing Speed Evaluator
spec: Assess typing test accuracy. The function `evaluate(users, expected)` maps user names to sequences of typed words, alongside a sequence of expected words. Extract all tested user names by iterating through the keys. Process each user by iterating over the users and their typed words. Compare words by iterating over a sequence of indices up to the length of the expected words. Count exact matches and case insensitive matches, treating missing typed words as errors. Find the maximum exact match count achieved by iterating through the results dictionary values. Return a tuple containing the results mapping, the list of user names, and the maximum exact match count.

title: Astronomy Star Catalog Matcher
spec: Identify overlapping astronomical observations. The function `starmatch(catalog, observations)` maps known star identifiers to spatial coordinate tuples, and new observation identifiers to spatial coordinate tuples. List all known star identifiers by extracting the catalog keys. Extract all distinct spatial coordinates from both sets by iterating through both dictionaries values. Process the matches by iterating over the catalog and the observations items. Compute the distance between every pair by iterating over a sequence of spatial dimensions based on the length of the coordinate tuples. If the distance is under five units, record a match. Return a tuple containing the matches dictionary mapping known stars to lists of observations, the list of star identifiers, and the distinct coordinates list.

title: City Block Distance Matrix
spec: Compute walking distances along city blocks. The function `distances(locations)` maps location names to tuples of integer horizontal and vertical grid coordinates. List all location names by extracting the keys. Find the minimum and maximum horizontal coordinates by iterating through the locations values. Create a grid density profile by iterating over a sequence of horizontal coordinates from the minimum to the maximum inclusive, counting how many locations exist at each coordinate. Compute the block distance between every possible pair of locations by iterating over pairs. Store distances in a mapping of tuple pairs to integers. Return a tuple containing the distances mapping, the location names list, and the grid density profile.

title: Lottery Ticket Checker
spec: Evaluate lottery ticket results. The function `lottery(tickets, winning)` maps player names to sequences of chosen ticket numbers, and provides the winning numbers. List all participating player names by extracting the keys. Evaluate tickets by iterating over the players and their tickets items. Check numbers by iterating over a sequence of indices corresponding to each ticket's length. Calculate prizes based on match counts. Find the highest prize awarded by iterating through the calculated prize dictionary values. Finally, generate a frequency distribution of all chosen numbers by iterating over a sequence of numbers from one to fifty, counting occurrences across all tickets. Return a tuple containing the prize dictionary, the player names list, the highest prize, and the frequency distribution.

title: Video Game Inventory Crafter
spec: Determine the maximum number of items a player can craft. The function `craft(inventory, recipes)` maps current inventory items to quantities, and craftable items to recipes (ingredient to quantity). List all available inventory items by extracting the keys. Extract all available quantities by iterating through the inventory values. Process recipes by iterating over the craftable items and their recipes. Calculate the maximum crafts by finding the minimum ratio of inventory to required amounts for each ingredient. Furthermore, calculate the total raw resources needed for bulk crafting by iterating over a sequence of batch quantities from one to ten for every recipe. Return a tuple containing the maximum crafts dictionary, the available items list, the available quantities list, and the bulk resource totals.

title: Knitting Pattern Generator
spec: Generate a grid of knitting symbols. The function `knit(stitches, rows)` maps stitch names to single character symbols, and row indices to primary stitch names. List all defined stitch names by extracting the stitches keys. Collect all distinct symbols used by iterating through the stitches values. Construct a grid of twenty rows and fifteen columns. Build the pattern by iterating over a sequence of twenty rows. For each row, determine the primary stitch from the rows dictionary. Fill the columns by iterating over a sequence of fifteen columns. Use the primary stitch, unless the column index exactly matches the row index, in which case use an edge stitch. Return a tuple containing the grid as a list of strings, the stitch names list, and the distinct symbols list.

title: Beehive Honey Production
spec: Calculate weekly honey production from beehive visit logs. The function `honey(hives)` maps hive identifiers to sequences of daily flower visit counts over a week. List all registered hive identifiers by extracting the keys. Extract all unweighted visit sequences by iterating through the values. Process each hive by iterating over the hives items. Calculate weighted honey yield for each hive by iterating over a sequence of seven days, multiplying the daily visit count by an efficiency weight that equals the day index plus one. Sum these to get the final yield. Return a tuple containing the weighted yields dictionary, the hive identifiers list, and the list of unweighted visit sequences.

title: Pixel Region Color Extractor
spec: Extract and analyze rectangular regions from a color grid. The function `pixels(image, patches)` maps coordinate tuples to color strings, and region names to definition tuples containing horizontal start, vertical start, width, and height. List all defined region names by extracting the patches keys. Identify all unique colors present in the entire image by iterating through the image values. Process each region by iterating over the patches items. Scan the defined area by iterating over sequences of horizontal and vertical offsets up to the defined width and height. Count color occurrences within the area, assuming missing coordinates are transparent, and find the most frequent color. Return a tuple containing the region color mapping, the region names list, and the unique colors list.

title: Movie Revenue Projector
spec: Forecast movie ticket revenues across multiple weeks. The function `project(theaters, multipliers)` maps theater names to initial opening week revenue, and week numbers to retention multipliers. List all tracked theater names by extracting the keys. Extract all initial opening week revenues by iterating through the theaters values. Process each theater by iterating over the theaters items. Project the revenue for eight weeks by iterating over a sequence of weeks from two to eight. Multiply the previous week's revenue by the appropriate multiplier, defaulting to zero point five if missing, and sum the total. Return a tuple containing the total revenue projections dictionary, the theater names list, and the initial revenues list.

title: Student Academic Profiler
spec: Takes a dictionary mapping student identifiers to their subject grade dictionaries, and a dictionary of subject credit values. Calculate the weighted grade point average for each student. Generate a dictionary of grade point averages rounded to the nearest integer mapped to the count of students with that average. Identify subjects that have no enrolled students. Rank the students by their average. Generate a sequence of integers from zero to four to format the top five student strings. Return a tuple containing a list of histogram frequencies, a list of empty subjects, and the formatted top student strings. The entry point is `profile(records, credits)`.

title: Minefield Clue Generator
spec: Takes a two dimensional list of characters representing a grid where asterisks are mines and dots are empty spaces. Calculate the number of neighboring mines for every empty space by inspecting adjacent row and column offsets. Create a frequency map of the generated numeric clues. Scan the frequency map to find the most common clue number and list any clue numbers from zero to eight that do not appear in the grid. Return a tuple of the solved two dimensional list, the highest frequency clue, and the list of missing clues. The entry point is `sweep(grid)`.

title: Polynomial Expression Evaluator
spec: Takes a list of dictionaries where each dictionary represents a polynomial, mapping integer exponents to integer coefficients. Multiply all polynomials sequentially into a single product dictionary. Compute the formal derivative of the product dictionary. Evaluate the product at five consecutive integer points starting from a given point. Determine the highest degree present in the product and extract all missing intermediate degrees from zero up to the maximum degree. Return a list containing the evaluated sum list, the evaluated derivative list of coefficients, and the list of missing degrees. The entry point is `evaluate(polynomials, point)`.

title: Spatial Filter Applier
spec: Takes a two dimensional grid of numbers and a smaller two dimensional grid representing a filter kernel. Apply the kernel to every valid position in the main grid to produce a new grid of reduced dimensions. Track the frequency of all resulting values in a dictionary. Find the maximum value in the new grid and sum the values in the kernel itself by examining its coordinates. Extract the unique resulting values and identify the one that occurs most frequently. Return the newly computed grid and the most frequent value. The entry point is `convolve(image, kernel)`.

title: Genetic Sequence Aligner
spec: Takes two strings representing biological sequences and integer scores for match, mismatch, and gap penalties. Construct a dynamic programming scoring matrix. Initialize the first row and first column using the gap penalty. Fill the remaining cells by evaluating the match, mismatch, and gap options for each position. Track the frequency of each chosen operation in a dictionary. Extract the final alignment score and identify the operation that was selected most often. Return a tuple containing the maximum alignment score and a list of all operations whose frequency exceeded five. The entry point is `align(primary, secondary, match, mismatch, gap)`.

title: Number Grid Checker
spec: Takes a two dimensional list representing a partially filled nine by nine puzzle grid. Verify that each row contains unique digits and each column contains unique digits. Verify that each three by three subgrid contains unique digits. Count the occurrences of each digit from one to nine across the entire grid. Identify any digits that are completely missing and any digits that appear more than nine times. Return a tuple indicating whether the grid is structurally valid and a list of any overused digits. The entry point is `verify(grid)`.

title: Node Coloration Validator
spec: Takes a dictionary mapping node identifiers to lists of neighboring nodes, and a dictionary mapping node identifiers to color integers. Verify that no two adjacent nodes share the same color. Count the number of nodes assigned to each color. Determine the maximum color integer used and identify all unused colors between zero and the maximum color. Count how many neighbors each node has and build a histogram of these degrees, then extract the most common degree. Return a tuple with a boolean indicating validity, the list of unused colors, and the most common degree. The entry point is `validate(graph, colors)`.

title: Storage Container Packer
spec: Takes a list of item weight and value pairs, and an integer maximum weight capacity. Use a dynamic programming approach to find the combination of items that maximizes total value without exceeding the capacity. Build a table of maximum values for every weight limit up to the maximum capacity. Backtrack through the table to determine exactly which items were chosen. Tally the frequencies of the chosen weights in a dictionary. Extract the weights that were used more than once. Return the maximum total value achieved and a list of heavily used weights. The entry point is `pack(items, capacity)`.

title: Prose Metrics Calculator
spec: Takes a string containing multiple sentences separated by periods. Split the text into words and compute their lengths. Build a dictionary mapping each word length to the count of words having that length. Build another dictionary mapping each unique word to its frequency. Find the longest word length and determine all lengths from one to the maximum length that have zero words. Identify all words that appear more than three times. Return a tuple of the average word length, the list of missing lengths, and a list of highly frequent words. The entry point is `analyze(text)`.

title: Transit Line Overlaps
spec: Takes a dictionary mapping bus line identifiers to lists of station names. Compute an inverse mapping of station names to the list of bus lines that stop there. Identify all stations that serve exactly one bus line and all stations that serve more than three bus lines. For each bus line, determine the length of its route. Find the maximum route length and generate a sequence of route positions from zero to the maximum to build a timetable template. Return a tuple containing the list of busy stations, the isolated stations, and the timetable template list. The entry point is `inspect(routes)`.

title: Paragraph Justification Formatter
spec: Takes a list of word strings and an integer line width. Group the words greedily into lines such that the total length of words and minimum spaces does not exceed the width. For each line, distribute remaining spaces as evenly as possible between words. Track the number of extra spaces added to each line in a dictionary. Count how many lines required zero extra spaces, how many required one, and so forth. Identify the maximum extra spaces used on any single line and list all integer space counts below that maximum that never occurred. Return the justified list of strings and the missing space counts. The entry point is `format(words, width)`.

title: Keystroke Effort Measurer
spec: Takes a text string. Precompute the physical coordinates of every character on a standard keyboard layout using a coordinate dictionary. Calculate the total physical distance a finger would travel to type the text. Tally the distances between consecutive characters into distance brackets, mapping bracket integers to counts. Find the most frequent distance bracket. Identify the longest sequence of consecutive identical characters by examining adjacent positions in the string. Find any distance brackets between zero and the maximum distance that have no occurrences. Return the total distance and the most frequent distance bracket. The entry point is `measure(text)`.

title: Bipartite Pairing Solver
spec: Takes a dictionary mapping participant names to lists of acceptable task identifiers. Find a maximal matching assigning each participant to exactly one acceptable task. Keep track of the final assignments in a dictionary. Identify any tasks that were requested by multiple participants but only assigned to one. Count the number of unassigned participants and the number of unassigned tasks. Produce a list of task identifiers grouped by how many participants initially requested them. Return a list of final assignment pairs and the list of unassigned participants. The entry point is `match(preferences)`.

title: Kiosk Change Maker
spec: Takes an integer target amount and a list of available integer coin denominations. Build a dynamic programming array to determine the minimum number of coins required for every amount from zero up to the target. Reconstruct the combination of coins used to reach the target exactly. Tally the quantity of each coin denomination used in a dictionary. Find denominations that were provided in the list but not used in the solution. Return the minimum total coins, a list of the used coin quantities, and the unused denominations. The entry point is `dispense(amount, coins)`.

title: Cinema Review Aggregator
spec: Takes a list of dictionaries where each dictionary represents a single movie and maps critic names to their numerical ratings. Calculate the overall average rating for every movie. Calculate the average rating given by each individual critic across all movies they reviewed. Build a dictionary mapping each possible rating integer from one to ten to the number of times it was given. Identify which critic was the most prolific and which integer rating was the most common. Return the highest rated movie and the most prolific critic. The entry point is `summarize(reviews)`.

title: Markup Structure Validator
spec: Takes a string containing simplified text markup tags. Extract all opening and closing tags in the order they appear. Use a stack to verify that tags are properly nested and matched. Keep a dictionary counting the occurrences of each tag type. Determine the maximum nesting depth reached during the parsing process. Generate a sequence of depth levels from zero to the maximum depth and count how many tags were closed at each level. Return a boolean indicating validity, a list of tag frequencies, and the deepest tag type. The entry point is `parse(document)`.

title: Ten Pin Scorer
spec: Takes a list of integers representing the number of pins knocked down in each roll. Traverse the rolls frame by frame to compute the total score for a standard ten frame game, properly accounting for strikes and spares. Keep a dictionary mapping each frame number to its total score contribution. Calculate the frequency of each score contribution value. Identify any frames that contributed exactly zero points. Generate a sequence of possible bonus points from one to three to simulate hypothetical perfect end games. Return the final total score, the highest scoring frame number, and the list of unique contribution values. The entry point is `score(rolls)`.

title: Parking Lot Tracker
spec: Takes an integer total capacity and a list of tuples containing timestamp, action string, and vehicle identifier. Simulate the arrival and departure of vehicles over time. Track the vehicles currently parked using a dictionary. Maintain a dictionary mapping each hour to the number of vehicles parked at that time. Find the peak occupancy hour. Identify any hours from zero to twenty three where the lot was completely empty. Calculate the total revenue by iterating over a sequence of hourly rates from one to five. Return the peak hour, the maximum occupancy reached, and a list of vehicles that never left. The entry point is `simulate(capacity, events)`.

title: Noughts Crosses Solver
spec: Takes a three by three list of strings representing a game board. Determine if there is a winner by checking all rows, all columns, and both diagonals. Count the occurrences of each symbol in a dictionary. Find all empty coordinate pairs on the board. Generate a sequence of integers corresponding to the empty cells and simulate placing the next player's symbol in each. Generate a heatmap grid counting how many winning combinations pass through each cell. Return a tuple containing the winner string if one exists, the number of empty cells, and a list of coordinates that would instantly result in a win. The entry point is `solve(board)`.

title: Climate Pattern Modeler
spec: Takes a list of observed weather state strings and an integer number of days to predict. Construct a transition frequency dictionary mapping each state to another dictionary of subsequent states. Convert these frequencies to a basic predictive model. Simulate the weather for the given number of days starting from the last observed state. Track the frequency of each simulated state. Identify any states from the original observation that never occurred in the simulation. Evaluate the sequence of observations using an integer index to build the transition map. Return the sequence of simulated states and the most frequent simulated state. The entry point is `predict(observations, days)`.

title: Roman Numeral Calculator
spec: Takes a list of strings representing ancient numerals. Convert each string to its integer equivalent by processing characters left to right and comparing adjacent values. Sum all the integer values. Convert the total sum back into a numeral string. Maintain a dictionary tallying the frequency of each character used in the final sum string. List any valid characters that do not appear in the final sum. Iterate over a sequence of indices to process the input strings correctly. Return the total integer, the final numeral string, and the most frequently used character in the result. The entry point is `calculate(numerals)`.

title: Matrix Determinant Calculator
spec: Takes a two dimensional list of numbers representing a square matrix. Calculate the determinant recursively using Laplace expansion. Base cases should handle singular values and small matrices. During the expansion, construct smaller submatrices by excluding specific rows and columns. Keep a dictionary mapping the size of each submatrix processed to the number of times a submatrix of that size was evaluated. Find the most common submatrix size processed. Check the main diagonal by iterating over an index sequence. Return the determinant and a list of frequencies for each submatrix size. The entry point is `determinant(matrix)`.

title: String Hash Collision Finder
spec: Takes a long text string and an integer window size. Compute a rolling hash for every substring of the given window size. Maintain a dictionary mapping each hash value to a list of starting indices where it occurred.
